families.title: Real positive-definite counterexamples to extended q-permanent monotonicity
families.summary: For every real parameter q>1, a real symmetric positive-definite matrix has a negative q-permanent derivative at q. An explicit matrix of order five decreases from q=14 to q=15. Correlation matrices with no zero entries and integer-entry examples are also obtained. The dimension can depend on q. The real-symmetric question on [−1,1] remains outside the result.

families.title: Gyires's permanent inequality for structured matrices
families.kind: Structured matrix inequalities and related polynomial bounds
families.summary: The preprint includes nonnegative circulants of orders five, six, and seven; all-order permutation polynomials aI+bQ+cQ²; all-order four-block matrices; one exceptional column or row; and all rank-at-most-two doubly stochastic matrices through order fifteen. It also proves structural, scalar, polynomial, deletion, balancing, local, and counting results. Exact counterexamples identify failed auxiliary assertions. The principal order-five and order-six claims, the all-order permutation-polynomial theorem, the all-order four-block theorem, and the exceptional-vector theorem have complete Lean proofs. General permanent comparisons and direct-sum closure also have Lean proofs. The rank-two result has a complete Lean proof for orders 2 through 5. The principal order-seven result and rank-two orders 6 through 15 remain incomplete in Lean. The unrestricted conjecture remains outside these results.
families.source: Gyires, 1978; Cheon and Wanless, 2005, Conjecture 20. Earlier formalization at the pinned Gyires repository.
families.formal_scope: The selected Comparator statements cover order-five circulants, the all-order four-block theorem, and the exceptional-vector theorem for n ≥ 2. Separate Lean packages prove the general order-six and all-order permutation-polynomial theorems. General permanent comparisons and direct-sum closure are also proved in Lean. The rank-two theorem has a complete Lean proof for orders 2 through 5. The principal order-seven theorem and rank-two orders 6 through 15 remain incomplete in Lean.

families.title: An entropy increase for a structurally disassortative DomiRank graph
families.kind: Counterexample to an interval monotonicity conjecture
families.summary: A connected graph with 14 vertices and 32 edges has negative degree–log-degree edge covariance. All resolvent scores are positive on [251/1000,63/250] inside the stable domain. Its entropy nevertheless increases by more than 1/10000 in natural-logarithm units. This refutes the source’s assertion for every positive-score interval.

families.title: Diagonal concavity does not imply concavity for sums of elementary symmetric polynomials
families.summary: For positive M, let f=1+Mσ₁+σ₂+Mσ₃+σ₄ in four variables. Its fourth root is concave on the positive diagonal exactly when M≥1. It is concave on the full positive orthant exactly when M=1. Every M>1 therefore disproves Lachaume’s diagonal criterion with strictly positive coefficients.

families.title: Sharp root log-concavity of alternating Motzkin sums
families.kind: Conjecture resolution with an optimal threshold
families.summary: Let Tₙ be the alternating sum of Motzkin numbers through index n. The sequence Tₙ^(1/n) is strictly log-concave on its tail starting at five. The inequality reverses at center five, so no earlier tail is log-concave. This strengthens Zhao’s proposed tail starting at nine. The source recurrence and finite sum are linked in Lean.
families.source: Zhao, INTEGERS 26 (2026), A55, Conjecture 1; OEIS A187306.

families.title: Counterexamples to a late-iterate ordering conjecture for generalized Hofstadter functions
families.summary: For every k≥4, some input n satisfies Fₖ^(2k+1)(n)>Fₖ₊₁^(2k+2)(n). The proof constructs inverse iterates whose exact gap is k−3. The finite witness F₄⁹(132)=8>7=F₅¹⁰(132) gives the first instance. The result concerns infinitely many parameters, not infinitely many violating inputs for each fixed parameter.
families.source: Letouzey, Li, and Steiner, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), 26.3.3, conjecture before Lemma 7.6.

families.title: Counterexamples to a best-of-n win-rate bound at every budget
families.kind: Disproof for every budget n≥2 and every positive atom cap
families.summary: For every n≥2 and δ>0, there is a finite positive reference distribution whose largest atom is at most δ and whose best-of-n policy violates the proposed divergence–win-rate curve. A four-response best-of-two example gives exact probabilities and a strict logarithmic certificate. The proof uses finite interval bounds and gives a quantitative positive gap. It does not determine the sharp replacement curve.
families.source: Beirami et al., ICML 2025, Conjecture 7.2 and equation (28).

families.title: Logarithmic influence bounds and variance counterexamples for Boolean decision-tree covariance
families.kind: Finite covariance bounds and variance counterexamples
families.summary: For finite Boolean decision trees with no repeated coordinate on a root-to-leaf path, a logarithmic influence bound controls signed and absolute tree covariance. A known family attains equality at powers of two. Exact read-3 examples disprove the proposed coefficient-one variance replacement, including an example in which every query is relevant. No Fourier entropy theorem is formalized.
families.source: Wan, Wright, and Wu, ITCS 2014, Section 2.4; Shalev, arXiv:1806.03646v2, Section 6.2.

families.title: A three-state thermal counterexample to a heat-current kurtosis conjecture
families.summary: A three-state two-temperature thermal rate model satisfies local detailed balance and has an exact negative fourth-to-second cold-heat spectral cumulant ratio. Lean checks the finite matrices, complex spectrum, a smooth locally dominant eigenvalue branch, and the exact derivative ratio. It does not formalize the stochastic long-time identification theorem.

families.title: The sharp level-one Fourier weight at density one eighth
families.summary: For every Boolean indicator of mean 1/8 on a finite uniform cube, the level-one Fourier weight is at most 3/64. A codimension-three subcube attains the bound in every dimension at least three.
families.source: Yu, On Average Distance, Level-1 Fourier Weight, and Chang’s Lemma, 2026 revision.
families.formal_scope: The formal proof includes arbitrary dimensions, the exact moment identities, the Hamming-distance bound, and sharpness witnesses.

families.title: Ultra-log-concavity of domination sequences of powers of paths and cycles
families.summary: The domination counts of every natural power of a path or cycle form an ultra-log-concave sequence. The proof includes all natural graph orders and powers, the binomial normalization, and the boundary graph cases.
families.formal_scope: Actual finite graph domination counts for powers of paths and cycles. No theorem for arbitrary graphs or real-rootedness is asserted.

families.title: Universal entanglement embezzlement with inverse-quadratic logarithmic infidelity
families.kind: Universal catalyst with a quantitative error bound
families.summary: A target-independent catalyst with local dimension 2^(4L) gives root infidelity at most 125m/L² for every Schmidt probability vector on m entries.
families.source: Van Dam and Hayden, 2003; Leung and Wang, 2014.
families.formal_scope: The proof constructs local basis permutations and establishes their finite complex Hilbert-space interpretation. Arbitrary changes to an external Schmidt basis are not separately formalized.

families.title: The exact asymmetric Merino–Welsh region for finite matroids
families.summary: The theorem characterizes all nonnegative pairs (x,y) for which T_M(x,0) T_M(0,y) ≥ T_M(1,1)² holds for every finite matroid without loops or coloops.
families.source: Liu, 2026; Chen and Xie, 2026. The manuscript states the relation to the diagonal theorem.
families.formal_scope: The statement uses actual Mathlib matroids and the literal subset rank sum. It includes empty ground sets and finite ground sets in arbitrary ambient types.

families.title: A sum-of-squares proof of the four-qubit Higuchi–Sudbery entropy bound
families.summary: The average von Neumann entropy of the three two-qubit marginals of a pure four-qubit state is at most log(2) + log(3)/2. The Higuchi–Sudbery state attains this bound.
families.formal_scope: The proof uses all sixteen complex amplitudes, actual reduced-matrix eigenvalues, an exact sum-of-squares identity, and an explicit maximizing state.

families.title: A quartic entropy deficit for random rankings
families.kind: Entropy deficit from pairwise comparison bias
families.summary: A distribution on rankings of n labels has entropy at most (1 − ε⁴/144) log(n!) if every pairwise comparison has probability at distance at least ε > 0 from 1/2.
families.source: Acan, Devlin, and Kahn, 2019; the manuscript identifies the established entropy arguments.
families.formal_scope: The proof includes all finite sizes and actual position-valued permutations. It assumes neither independent comparisons nor transitive preferred directions.

research_notes.title: Supporting records for the all-order Gyires arguments
research_notes.status: The four-block and permutation-polynomial theorems have complete Lean proofs. The written proofs and exact certificates remain available. No first-priority or independent human expert review claim is made.

research_notes.title: Supporting records for the complete Gyires preprint
research_notes.status: Ordinary proofs and exact certificates. Broader Lean verification, novelty assessment, and independent human expert review remain incomplete.
